market_context: United States and Canada; practical, safety-first household guidance written natively for North American readers.
title: How Long Can Eggs Sit Out?

seo.title: How Long Can Eggs Sit Out?
seo.meta_description: In the U.S., refrigerated eggs should generally not sit at room temperature for more than about two hours. Handling practices differ by country.
seo.search_intent: Determine how long normally refrigerated eggs can stay out and understand why egg-storage guidance differs between markets.

excerpt: Eggs are not marketed the same way everywhere. In the U.S. and other refrigerated supply chains, keep eggs cold and do not leave them on the counter for hours.
content_html:
For eggs sold and stored refrigerated, a practical limit is about two hours at room temperature. In very hot conditions, the safe window is shorter.

The commercial handling system matters

In the United States, eggs are commercially washed and kept refrigerated. In many European markets they are sold unrefrigerated. Do not mix rules from different supply chains.

If they arrived cold, keep them cold

Temperature swings can create condensation on the shell. Store refrigerated eggs in their carton in a stable part of the refrigerator.

Cooking does not erase an unknown temperature history

If eggs sat out for many hours and you cannot reconstruct the time, discarding them is safer than trying to compensate with extra cooking.

The float test is not a safety test

Floating can reflect the size of the egg’s air cell and therefore age, but it does not detect dangerous bacteria.

If you live where eggs are routinely sold unrefrigerated, follow local public-health and package guidance; the two-hour rule here applies to eggs in a refrigerated supply chain.

faq.question: Why are eggs unrefrigerated in some countries?
faq.answer: Processing and supply-chain practices differ; follow the safety system used where you buy them.

faq.question: Does the float test prove an egg is safe?
faq.answer: No. It can indicate age but does not detect pathogens.

faq.question: Can I refrigerate eggs again after they sat out?
faq.answer: Yes after a short period within the safe window; discard them when they were out for hours or the time is unknown.
